page: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache. Vector and matrix acceleration features include AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions (amx_tile and amx_int8). Hardware acceleration is limited to the CPU, as the system includes zero GPUs.

A defining characteristic of this configuration is its high memory-to-vCPU ratio. With 512.0 GB of RAM across 16 vCPUs, the server allocates 32.0 GB of memory per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring all persistent storage to be attached remotely via Azure Premium Storage. Memory bandwidth reaches 132.03 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 90.18 GB/sec for uncached writes, while cached 16 KB read throughput registers at 1241.41 GB/sec.

Benchmark results show balanced compute output alongside strong memory and single-threaded performance. Single-core processing achieves strong marks, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and gzip compression throughput of 31.31 GB/sec. Multi-core performance remains moderate due to the 16-vCPU footprint, recording 15978.86 in stress-ng and 12457.0 in Geekbench. In machine learning benchmarks, small 135M model text generation achieves 288.15 tokens/sec, while 7B model generation operates at 12.6 tokens/sec.

Cost efficiency is focused around memory-intensive software licensing models. By constraining the core count to 16 vCPUs while retaining the full 512.0 GB memory footprint of an E64-class host, this instance helps reduce licensing fees tied to CPU core counts. The primary operational tradeoff is the lack of local NVMe storage and reliance on networked storage for disk I/O. The system is well fitted for in-memory databases like Redis, large SAP and relational database instances, memory-heavy analytics, and ETL processes.
